profile.reading:
Per CoreSite's own facility page, this building, AT2, is located at 1130 Powers Ferry Place, Marietta, GA 30067; despite CoreSite's own URL slug and page branding calling it "AT2 Atlanta," the confirmed street address places the building in Marietta, Cobb County, not the city of Atlanta itself, and this entry uses the accurate Marietta location rather than the marketing label. CoreSite publishes 67,000-plus square feet for this building. No MW capacity or opening year is stated. CoreSite lists SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA compliance for its facilities generally.

CoreSite is a subsidiary of American Tower Corporation (NYSE: AMT), which completed its acquisition of CoreSite in late 2021; Stonepeak Partners LP separately acquired roughly 29% of American Tower's US data center business in July 2022, later increased to about 36%. Georgia has separately drawn intense hyperscale investment, with Georgia Power forecasting demand growth from roughly 400 megawatts to nearly 10,000 megawatts of data center-driven load and the state offering a $296 million sales tax exemption program for large data center projects, per Atlanta Journal-Constitution and Atlanta Tech News reporting, a very different scale of activity than this Cobb County interconnection-focused CoreSite building represents.

American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite driving stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results, projecting data-center segment revenue of $1.20 billion to $1.22 billion for full-year 2026, roughly 14.9% growth at the midpoint, and raising its full-year outlook on the strength of that performance; the company also budgeted approximately $695 million in data-center development spending for 2026, funding continued build-out across CoreSite's 11-market US portfolio.

reading.body:
CoreSite AT2 publishes 67,000 square feet of technical space but no power figure, making it impossible to assess its contribution to AI infrastructure without assumptions the operator has not supplied.

The 67,000-square-foot footprint places AT2 in the mid-sized colocation range, suitable for enterprise workloads but not in the hyperscale category now driving AI compute deployment. Without a megawatt figure, the square footage alone cannot translate to racks, GPU density, or AI training capacity. That gap matters because power density varies by workload and cooling design, and the operator chose not to publish either.

The facility holds six compliance certifications spanning financial services, payment processing, health data, information security, and federal security standards. These qualifications serve regulated enterprises and their data but do not signal readiness for large-scale AI training. AI infrastructure specifications like power redundancy tier, cooling architecture, and GPU-to-rack configuration are absent from the published profile.

Georgia's index shows 33 facilities statewide, but only 2 publish megawatt figures, totaling 42 MW combined. AT2's missing power data means Georgia appears as a thin compute picture for AI, and whether AT2 adds materially to that figure remains unknown. For readers tracking grid constraints on AI scaling, a state where the largest facilities hide their power consumption is a state that has not yet made its capacity visible to the market.
